text: To proactively manage trade surplus to mitigate risks in international trade: the Government

Under the Government's Resolution No. 403/NQ-CP, signed by Permanent Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc on November 21, 2026, a comrehensive plan for managing trade surplus and mitigating risks in international trade activities for the period 2026 - 2030 has been approved.
The plan's objective is to consistently implement tasks and solutions to manage trade surplus in bilateral relations proactively and sustainably.

It aims to harmonize the expansion of exports and the enhancement of import capacity for production, improve the quality and added value of exported goods, and simultaneously prevent the risk of overcapacity, illegal transshipment, origin fraud, and effectively enforce regulations on banning the import of goods produced by forced labor.

Under the plan, managing trade surplus is linked with diversifying markets and supply sources, increasing localization rates and domestic added value, enhancing the resilience of supply chains, ensuring fair trade, and limiting risks arising from trade imbalances, excessive export concentration, or over-dependence on certain markets, products, and input sources.
Agencies will monitor and provide early warnings on the scale, structure, and concentration of trade surplus in product groups, markets, and enterprises with large turnover or surplus.

Proactively identifying factors causing trade barriers, illegal transshipment, overcapacity, or forced labor helps protect the reputation, enhance transparency, and competitiveness of Vietnamese goods.
Simultaneously, the plan assigns specific tasks to each ministry, sector, and locality as a basis for building action programs, enhancing information sharing, inspection, and handling violations.
To achieve the above objectives, the Government requires focusing on implementing seven main solutions:

First: Perfecting the institutional management of trade surplus, goods origin, C/O, self-certification, and post-inspection; strengthening inspection and verification of high-risk items and supply chains associated with early warning mechanisms for large surplus groups prone to illegal transshipment.
Functional agencies increase information exchange with importing countries and review input sources under warning about forced labor, controlling strategic exports.

Second: Managing trade surplus based on data and risk management by connecting customs, tax, investment, import-export, and production data; building a database of origin and supply chains; and analyzing the import-export structure, especially the contribution of foreign-invested enterprises, to assess sustainability.

Third: Strengthening supply chains, increasing added value, and import capacity for production by developing supporting industries, enhancing FDI linkages with domestic enterprises, and increasing localization rates.

The state encourages the import of new machinery and technology and supports forming intra-regional supply chains to take advantage of tariff preferences from signed free trade agreements and limit the risk of being accused of overcapacity, illegal transshipment, and forced labor in exports.

Fourth: Managing planning, investment, and capacity according to market signals, ensuring production meets domestic and international demand and absorption capacity, proactively preventing overcapacity in major export sectors.
Fifth: Reviewing tax, land, investment, credit incentives, and export support policies to adjust regulations that easily cause overcapacity or subsidy risks, in line with international commitments.
Sixth: Perfecting mechanisms to identify and control goods, areas, and suppliers at risk of using forced labor, increasing verification with foreign countries to enforce import bans.

Seventh: Enhancing coordination and enforcement capacity through clear responsibility assignment, resource allocation, staff training, and regularly reporting to the Government on trade surplus and arising risks.
Controlling trade surplus, supply sources, and preventing origin fraud

In managing trade surplus, the Ministry of Industry and Trade leads in monitoring and periodically evaluating the scale and structure of trade surplus by industry, market, and enterprise area, and operates an early warning mechanism.

The Ministry of Finance coordinates in analyzing customs and investment data, identifying large export enterprises, evaluating the contribution of the FDI sector, and researching FDI capital regulation from the registration stage to diversify markets and automatically share investment data.
Regarding supply chains, the Ministry of Industry and Trade builds a database of input supply sources, reviews import dependency, and domestic added value in key export sectors.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade coordinates with the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Science and Technology, the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, the Ministry of Public Security, and the People's Committees of key FDI-attracting provinces and cities, and industry associations to exploit the traceability system, develop supporting industries, and increase localization rates.

To prevent origin fraud and illegal transshipment, the Ministry of Industry and Trade researches and proposes the Government issue a decree replacing Decree 31/2018/ND-CP dated March 8, 2018, on goods origin and proposes amendments to Decree 98/2020/ND-CP dated August 26, 2020, on administrative sanctions in trade and production of counterfeit goods and banned goods, and on consumer protection.

Along with upgrading the electronic C/O issuance system, connecting customs, tax, and investment data, and sharing information on self-certifying enterprises with the Customs Department, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Industry and Trade enhance staff capacity, support enterprises in responding to foreign trade defense investigations, and publish results of handling violations related to goods transshipment, origin fraud, and forced labor.

The Ministry of Finance implements Decree 169/2026/ND-CP dated May 15, 2026, on administrative sanctions in the customs field, tightening origin checks on large turnover items, training staff, and allocating funds for implementation according to the State Budget Law.

The Ministry of Public Security coordinates inspections of high-risk enterprises, handles origin fraud with criminal signs, perfects legal frameworks, and shares VNeID identification data to prevent evasion and tax avoidance.
Reviewing capacity, policies, labor, and foreign affairs

To limit overcapacity, the Ministry of Industry and Trade reviews sector planning, production targets associated with credit, land, and corporate income tax incentives; simultaneously raises technical, environmental, and energy efficiency standards to screen new small-scale, outdated technology projects.

The People's Committees of centrally-run provinces and cities coordinate with the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Industry and Trade, and the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment to review licensed projects under construction or in unimplemented planning, including FDI projects, and evaluate policies easily considered export subsidies.
The State Bank of Vietnam, together with the Ministry of Finance, reviews, explains, and proposes handling monetary and credit policies that risk creating unfair trade advantages.

Regarding the import ban on goods using forced labor, the Ministry of Home Affairs amends labor policies to protect workers' rights in line with international commitments, establishes verification mechanisms with foreign countries, and issues implementation guidelines.

New regulations allow identifying high-risk goods groups, areas, and suppliers, temporarily suspending customs clearance when there is evidence, requiring enterprises to prove material sources or refuse imports, and demanding re-export.

The Ministry of Finance updates data on wages, employment, living costs, and household living standards; the Ministry of Industry and Trade guides enterprises in digitizing management and tracing materials to avoid forced labor.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs leads coordination with the Ministry of Industry and Trade to enhance partner engagement, fully inform measures to promote balanced trade in Vietnam, clarify structural factors, and objective impacts from global supply chain shifts.
Both ministries and agencies closely monitor the situation to provide early warnings of investigation risks and adverse tax impositions to proactively advocate and handle promptly.
